source_user: Two serving systems claim different tokens/s. Design a reproducible comparison. Scenario variant 206: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: freeze model revision, tokenizer, precision, hardware, topology, prompt/generation distributions, concurrency, warmup, stopping rules, and telemetry; publish raw request traces.
corrected_answer: For variant 206, treat both headline rates as unverified until a shared measurement contract is applied. Define tokens/s as input, generated, and accepted tokens per wall-clock second, with exact request/first-token/completion timestamps and explicit inclusion of queueing, batch formation, retries, cancellations, failures, and network time. Freeze and record model and tokenizer revisions, precision, runtime and libraries, driver versions, hardware/topology/clocks, serving configuration, decoding and stop rules, prompt and target-length distributions, seeds, concurrency, admission/batching policy, cache state, warmup, duration, and network path. Replay identical randomized request blocks in paired crossover order at prespecified load levels, with repeated blocks sized to estimate confidence intervals. Falsifiable hypothesis: admission, batching, or queueing—not decoder execution—is the primary cause of the reported gap; after those controls are equalized, the gap will fall below a predeclared practical margin. Measure each token-rate definition, completed requests/s, TTFT, inter-token and end-to-end latency, queue time, p50/p95/p99, errors, timeouts, cancellations, utilization, memory, power/cost, correctness, and task quality. Publish versioned manifests, seeds, raw per-request traces, telemetry definitions, and analysis code; predeclare exclusions, stopping, uncertainty, and disconfirmation rules. Investigate thermal throttling, cache warming, clock drift, background load, scheduler and network contention, tokenizer mismatch, and missing telemetry. Canary any serving change and fail closed to the last known-good configuration if correctness, error rate, tail latency, resource/thermal limits, or telemetry integrity breach guardrails; obtain domain-expert review before operational rollout.
risks: Ambiguous token and timing definitions can invalidate comparison.

evidence_required: Versioned manifests and raw per-request traces for both systems.
